mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior 1 month period reduces the risk-free rate, lowering discount rates for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.10 percentage points over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0 percent over the prior 1 month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises above 4.0% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the prior 1 month period reflects broad-based economic contraction, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both PAYEMS and HOUST decline by more than 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 index level over the prior 1 month period signals manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate capital expenditure and earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO falls below 105.0 during a late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1300.0 thousand units over the prior 1 month period indicates weakening consumer demand for housing, reducing retail sales and corporate revenue growth, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST falls below 1300.0.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of CPIAUCSL above 250.0 (elevated inflation) and FEDFUNDS below 1.5% (accommodative policy) signals potential central bank delay in rate response, increasing the risk of sudden rate hikes that trigger negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 250.0 and FEDFUNDS is below 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the prior 1 month period indicates manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate capital expenditure and earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO declines by at least 0.5% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) below 495,000 million dollars over the prior 1 month period reflects weakening consumer spending, reducing corporate revenue growth and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS falls below 495,000.
